column1: # What has been swept, and when. One line per package or
# partial sweep, replaced each time it runs.
# read.tsv says why a survivor was left. This says what was looked at,
# which read.tsv cannot: a clean package leaves nothing in it.
# The last column is the one to read: survivors nobody has explained.
# Survived counts the error branches and the bounds that hold a value
# to itself as well, and on anything that lays out a screen or talks to
# Herdr for a living those are most of the list -- a package can survive
# seventeen and have nothing whatever to answer for.
# The four outcome columns account for every mutation, so a row that
# does not add up to its own first number is a row to distrust. They
# used to be two, and mutations minus caught minus survived was an
# unnamed remainder that could be either of the others.
# Rows dated before 2026-09-06 have no hung column and counted a suite
# that ran out of time as caught, so their caught is an upper bound.
